name: NJ-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+15 partisan lean strongly favors the incumbent party
Rob Menendez holds a decisive fundraising edge with over $2.2 million raised and outside support, while challengers show no reported finances
No Republican is on the ballot; independent and third-party challengers lack resources or visibility
Prediction markets price Democratic retention around 95%
model.rationale: The forecast rests on the district's strong Democratic lean, Menendez's incumbency and financial dominance, and the absence of a funded or major-party challenger. Markets and fundamentals both point to an easy Democratic hold, with no polls or ratings suggesting otherwise.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal tied to the incumbent or a surge in outside spending for the independent challengers could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Aristotle Eliopoulos is an independent standing in for the Republican side.

overview:
NJ-08, anchored in Hudson County, leans Democratic by fifteen points, and incumbent Rob Menendez returns after securing renomination. He enters the general election with a major financial advantage: more than $2.2 million raised, $722,000 on hand, and over $900,000 in outside support, with no recorded opposition spending against him.

His opponents face steep odds. Aristotle Eliopoulos, an independent standing in for the Republican side, along with two other minor challengers, report no fundraising. With no Republican nominee on the ballot and no public polling in the race, the fundamentals point firmly to the incumbent. Prediction markets price Democratic retention near 95%, consistent with a comfortable double-digit win in this safely Democratic seat.
